title: Cannonball Adderley's Big Man, Randy Crawford and Bob Guillaume
summary: Jones recalls arranging for Cannonball's Big Man while Cannon read the script at his house, plus work with Randy Crawford and Bob Guillaume.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: You worked on "Big Man" with Cannonball?
(Inaudible)
Yes.
What was your contribution to "Big Man"?
(Inaudible)

That was a -- let me go back awhile, now. Randy Crawford? I did the things for Randy Crawford, strings and woodwinds and all that, you know? Oh, yeah, when Johnny Guitar Watson -- I orchestrated his thing. But the biggest thing was that Cannonball used to come up to my house, right up here on Lookout Mountain, you know? And we had like a spiral staircase, you know, going down the side of the hill. And Cannon was a good actor in reading a script. So he kept coming by, because he wanted me to absorb the script, you know, as much as I could. And of course there were several arrangers. There was Tom MacIntosh, David Axelrod, oh -- I can't think of --
(Dave Blumberg - ed.)

Blumberg, with the Barry Gordy record company. So they had all these guys here, you know. But Cannon would come by the house and read it and he -- and my wife Speedy would go out and get all the kids, and they would sit on the spiral staircases, you know?
Uh-huh.

And when he saw the kids, oh boy, he would go into his act then. And he could really do it, you know. And then he got Joe Williams, and he imported somebody, some people. And Bob [Guillaume,] the one that I've been doing some work with here lately, you know?
What are you doing with him?
(Inaudible)
Just building his book, you know.
He's both an actor and a singer, is that right?

Yeah. And he's working on the -- I think he was Purlie in the show, "Purlie". And he's working on the TV show, "Soap." Yeah, he's pretty heavy. A great talent, strong talent. But Joe Williams did a good job in acting and reciting lines, too.
Joe's a good actor.
(Inaudible)
Yeah. He's a talent, you know.
Actually, anyone who does a song well is acting as well as singing.
(Inaudible)
Yeah, that's right.
He's an actor everytime he does a number, but that dramatic thing (Inaudible).
(Inaudible)
Yeah. Yeah, that was good.
